_readme: THE ONE REGISTRY. Paolo 9/14, LOCKED (laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_ONE_VOTE_TAB_AND_THE_PORTRAIT_CHAT_9_14_26.md).
There is ONE place he votes: the VOTE tab, behind the gear, in the demo. This file is what it reads.
It lives in records/target/ because that is one of the three folders GitHub Pages publishes (_config.yml),
so the tab can fetch it in production. slices/ and engine/ are the other two.
HOW A LANE REGISTERS A CANDIDATE: append one object to items[]. Never edit somebody else's object.
id     a unique slug. Never reused. A redo is a NEW id.
kind   song | sound | face | haircut | outfit | tile | animation | line | ui | verdict | redo
lane   the chat that made it
sha    the commit the thing landed in, so anyone can go look at it
made   the date it was made, as m/d
title  what he sees on the row, in plain words
why    one short line: what changed and what he is deciding
show   how to show it: {how:'page'|'image'|'clip'|'audio'|'text', src:'...'} .
page/image/clip/audio src is a path RELATIVE TO slices/ . text src is the words themselves.
redoOf (redos only) the id this one replaces
said   (redos only) his words on the one it replaces, quoted back so he is never judging blind
HOW A LANE READS A VERDICT BACK: look in verdicts[] for your id. up = build it in, down = graveyard
with a post-mortem (a clip is redone and comes back as a NEW id). NOTES ARE RULINGS: do not ask again.
A VOTE CONSUMES. An id that appears in verdicts[] NEVER renders in the tab again. The tab also
remembers his vote on the phone the moment he taps, so the row leaves before this file is updated.
gates/vote_tab_gate.js plants a judged id here and proves the tab refuses it.

items.title: THE FIRST PERSON AT YOUR DOOR, SPEAKING
items.why: The Meter Reader stops being a card and becomes somebody on your step. They have no name until you ask, and they dodge when you do. Read their opening, the three ways you can shape the deal, their yes, their no, and what they say when you come back.

  You are new on this block. That is useful to me.
  Six streets east there is a box that counts this block.
  I need the number off it. I cannot be seen there.

items.title: HOW A STEP IS DRAWN (I PICKED ONE FOR YOU)
items.why: One press moves him a whole house, 275 pixels, in half a second, and his legs can only show one pace of it. What shipped was nobody’s choice: an old number in the code made the whole street jump at once. I put in the tape skip: he stands still, the picture skips twice, he is there. Thumbs up keeps it. Thumbs down and say GRID (the street jumps at once) or SLIDE (the street slides the whole time) and I will switch it.

items.title: THE ROOM ON THE TAP
items.why: The first sound after you press the door. A low electrical hum with a faint hiss on top, so the game sounds like a place that still has power and nobody in it. Your heartbeat sound is unchanged and sits on top of it. Three things to call: how loud the room is under the heartbeat, whether it stays on once the song starts, and whether it should sound like it came through an old radio or like a room you are just standing in.

items.title: THE WATER STILL RUNS
items.why: The water authority's sign, still lit and still reporting to nobody. I checked the real valley: one crew holds every drop of running water and nothing has ever told you. Is this the right shape for an institution?

items.title: SOMEBODY ASKS YOU
items.why: Three real jobs the valley is offering right now, spoken by a person on your block instead of shown on a card. Vote the words.

items.title: THE FIGHT, JUDGED, ROUND 3
items.why: Three pictures side by side: the street you walk, the fight that starts there, and the fight's new floor rebuilt from your own street (checked piece by piece, it IS your street). The floor passed. Still wrong in the fight: the tiny fighter, the cold light, the chart clutter, the floating bar. Agree with the call, or is something else the worst thing?

items.title: THERE ARE NO KIDS AND NOBODY OLD
items.why: Every single person you walk past right now is a grown adult. The rig could always build a kid and an old man, and only one body in the whole game has ever used it. Here they are, standing next to a grown man at the same scale. Should the street have them?

items.title: YOU PAID IT
items.why: The other end of the cut-off notice. You pay, and the closing receipt lands on the phone with the zero written out, because a bill that just stops coming is not a receipt. It thanks you and tells you to keep it in case of a dispute, with nobody left to dispute it to.

items.title: THE STEP DROPS A FRAME
items.why: His legs have four drawings and one press moves him a whole house, so the legs can never cover it. They used to walk smoothly while the street jumped, which is the moonwalk. Now he holds still, the picture drops two frames, and he lands on the beat. Same four drawings, no new art. A short press does not skip, because there is no distance to show.

items.title: A FOOTSTEP THAT LANDS ON THE BEAT
items.why: Your old footsteps were almost pure tones, like a beep. A real footfall is mostly noise with a little weight under it. This one is noise-first and its loudest instant is right at the start, so the step lands ON the beat instead of just after it. Play it against the beat on the page.

items.title: THE STEP LOSES CONTACT
items.why: The same step, but the sound drops out twice mid-stride, like old tape losing its grip. It goes dull first and then quiet and never fully silent. The two drop-outs are timed to the exact moments the ground skips under you in the walk, so what you hear is what you see.

items.title: THE PHONE STILL TRANSMITS
items.why: What the phone sounds like when you open it. Two tones together that do not agree with each other, coming through a dead radio band. Then the tones stop and the hiss keeps going, because the transmitter is still on and nobody is at the other end.

items.title: THE STREET AT THREE HOURS
items.why: Your valley has 41 people outside at ten in the morning and 4 at eight at night, and your street draws 23 and 24. Same crowd at breakfast and at bedtime. Six real pictures off the glass, the day counted hour by hour, and three ways to go. An empty street at eight is free dread if you want it, or it reads as a bug. Your call.

items.title: THE BATTERY SHED, THE FIRST BUILDING THAT MAKES MONEY
items.why: You build this on your own lot and a battery comes in. It is the small one, about the size of half a garage, not the big fenced battery yard the game already has. I drew it in that yard’s own colours so they are the same world. One thing in the picture is on purpose and it is the whole idea: THE LITTLE AMBER LIGHT IS LIT. Nothing else on the lot has power, the meter needle is stuck, the door is chained, and this box is still working. Thumbs up and I put it in the game so you can place one. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the shape, the colour, or the light.

items.title: FIVE WAYS THE NOTES SECTION SITS
items.why: You could not find the notes control. It was the only thing in that bar with no plate. Here is the fix and four other ways, plus three shapes for the section itself.

items.title: THE BLOCK HOLDS THE DOOR
items.why: The eviction notice the landlord brings to your door, and the reason it can fail. Glasgow 1915: 25,000 families stopped paying and won, because the neighbours stood in the doorway and nobody could take the flat. Read the last line of the notice: it threatens you with a court that does not exist.

items.title: THE RULES RUN WITH THE DIRT
items.why: The homeowners association is still fining you. Every tract here is walled because the county made walls compulsory, and the rules that come with the wall are recorded against the land itself, so they never needed a city or a court to survive. The fine adds up daily and the hearing is before a board that stopped meeting years ago.

items.title: SHOULD PEOPLE BE DIFFERENT HEIGHTS?
items.why: Right now everybody in the game is the same height. The slider that is supposed to change it only moves a body 7 per cent, which nobody can see. Here is the same man short, normal and tall, at one scale with their feet on one line. Is that spread right, too much, or not enough? (The tall one's head is cut flat at the top. That is a real bug this picture found, not the look.)

items.title: ARGUING THE PRICE
items.why: Haggling over a job by talking to the person instead of tapping rows on a card. He warns you out loud before the push that costs you, then walks. Vote the words.

items.title: THE NOTICE AT THE EDGE
items.why: The board a crew nails up where its ground starts. Three tiers, three completely different rents, all read straight off the game. This is the first sign somebody alive made: hand painted, not printed.

items.title: A SONG THROUGH THE DEAD SPEAKER
items.why: This is the answer to your own sound call being changed, made into something you can hear. You said post-apocalyptic FFX; the analog horror rule now comes first, and the way to keep both is a warm tune arriving through a broken radio. The page plays the same tune twice: once clean, once through the speaker. Pick which one the game uses.

items.title: THE FOLD
items.why: The sound of a generation passing. Somebody stops, and the electrical hum of the house carries on at exactly the same pitch, because the grid does not care that a man died. Nothing swells and nothing rises. Tell me if that is too cold.

items.title: THE FIGHT'S CLOUD
items.why: You ruled that a cloud crosses the fight. A cloud makes no noise, so what you hear is what a cloud does to a place: the brightness goes out of the room and comes back. No whoosh, because a whoosh would be a sound effect pretending to be weather. It uses the same darkness numbers the city's own weather already uses.

items.title: THE DOOR
items.why: Walking through a door, and the real sound of it is not the hinge: it is one room becoming another. Outside is wide and inside is closed in and narrower, and the same electrical hum is on both sides because it is the same house. The latch is the small part.

items.title: FOUR WAYS THE GAME LOADS
items.why: The screen that covers everything before you can touch anything, with a bar that cannot lie and the writing chat’s words wired to real stages. A is built and handed to the play chat.

items.title: THE TURN TAKES THE BEAT
items.why: Right now there is no turn at all. Change direction and he is just a different drawing on the next frame: facing south, then facing east, nothing in between. He already has eight drawings, one per direction, so a turn is those drawings in order. He holds, swings through the one in between, and lands, the same half second the street takes. No new art. Not in the game until you say so.

items.title: THE ONE WHO WALKS WITH YOU
items.why: Nobody has ever walked beside you in this game: 0 of the 61 people on your block will follow you, and only an enemy is even allowed to. Here is the person your world picks, with her real face and name, what she wants and the one thing she will not do. You said shuffle, and the shuffle has one card, because only one person is ever close enough. Pick which reasons count.

items.title: THE SHOP IS STILL LIT, AND EVERY SHELF IN IT IS BARE
items.why: A corner store you can walk up to. Three bays, faded awnings, a blank sign out on the lot. Everything in the picture is boring on purpose except ONE thing: the middle shop still has its lights on. Two tubes are still burning in there and what they show you is seven empty shelf runs and a checkout stripped to the counter. A shop that is still open with nothing in it is worse than a dark one. I drew it in the shopping district's own colours so it is the same world you walk. Thumbs up and I build it into the street so you can walk up to a lit shop. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the shop, the light, or the empty shelves.

items.title: THEY TAKE THEIR SUNGLASSES OFF TO TALK TO YOU
items.why: 70 of every 200 people in the valley wear wraparound shades you cannot see through, and the face that pops up when they speak has always had bare eyes. The face drawing never knew glasses exist. Top row is the head on the street, then the portrait now, then the same portrait wearing the same shades in the colours that garment is actually painted in.

items.title: THE STREET GETS KIDS, BUT IT CANNOT GET OLD PEOPLE
items.why: Your twelve street people are all grown adults. Here they are again with ages dealt out in the shares Clark County really has: 1 kid, 1 teen, 2 young adults, 6 adults, 2 old people. The kid and the teen work. THE OLD PEOPLE DO NOT, and the strip at the top shows why: the game's young adult, adult and old man are the same body within 3 per cent. That 3 per cent is actually correct, real people barely shrink with age, which means you can never get an old man out of height. He needs a bent back and grey hair. So: do you want kids and teens on the street now, and should I go build a proper old man?

items.title: THE TWELVE GET AN END
items.why: People remember the last moment of a thing almost as much as the biggest one. Every roadside encounter already has an ending built, and not one of them had a word for it. Here they are.

show.src:
EVERY ROADSIDE MOMENT ALREADY HAS AN ENDING DESIGNED. NONE OF THEM HAS WORDS.

People remember an experience by its biggest moment and its LAST moment, and
almost not at all by how long it went on. We wrote the openings last round.
This is the other half.

  the dogs break        The rest went with him. They always go with him.
  the coyote leaves     It went. They do that once you look straight at it.
  the snake got you     Sit down. Ten minutes and you will know either way.

  the scavenger, three ways it can end
    you paid            Take it and go. I did not see which way you went.
    you scared him      He will tell people you scared him. That is worse.
    you dropped him     That one had a name on this street. People knew him.

  the toll, two ways
    you paid            Road is yours for the day. Nobody will stop you.
    you went around     Long way round, then. It adds an hour and it is safe.

  the snatcher got it   You are not getting that back. Let it go and walk.
  the mad one           You cannot pay that one. Nobody can. He is past it.
  the bounty squad      There will be more of them next week. There always are.
  the old casino bot    The alarm went out. Whoever owns this block heard it.
  the drone             Kill the light and the rest of them fall out of the air.
  the empty taxi        It will take you. It does not ask where you are going.
  two patrols fought    Neither of them won. Walk while they are still counting.

items.title: THE DAY THE MONEY DIES
items.why: Every purchase burns the battery, so the valley can be spent down to nothing. I drove it there: 56 batteries burned, zero left across 19 hands, shelves still full. This is the shop's price list on that morning. Every line is correct and every line is one battery and there is not one left.

items.title: THE MARK ON THE WALL
items.why: A crew's mark painted straight onto somebody else's wall. No words, no post. The bar is the crew, the point is which way they went, the strokes are how many. Does this grammar work for all fourteen?

items.title: THE HAND REACHES THE FACE
items.why: Five of the ones you killed have the same thing wrong and you named it yourself. His hand never actually gets to his face, and it lands somewhere different every time he turns, because all five were aiming with the helper the GUN clips use. His head is 22 pixels tall and his hand was about 20 pixels away from it. Redone: 9 pictures out of 40 read right before, 33 now. Not in the game yet, on purpose, because putting them in cuts his head off his body in profile.
items.redoOf: eat, drink, smoke, cough and whistle
items.said: a lot of them are good, a lot of them aren’t good... some of the DIRECTIONS look like dog shit: when it’s facing north-east the hand was behind the head even though it’s supposed to be in front. IF I KILLED IT I DON’T WANT IT GONE. Make a new one.

items.title: WHAT PEOPLE REPEAT ABOUT YOU
items.why: Two people can watch you put somebody down and it moves nothing, for ever. Your reputation table has 83 rows and all 83 are quest steps; the seven things your street can actually see you do are not in it. Here are the five things people repeat about a stranger, what each one costs, and what everything else is worth, which is nothing. One bad thing costs five good ones. Pick how harsh that is.

items.title: FOUR WAYS THE TOP BAR FITS
items.why: The bar you photographed running off your screen, with your own words in it, four ways. B is built. Plus the phone as its own button.

items.title: THE TAPE IS SLIPPING
items.why: The same tune through the same broken radio, but now the machine playing it is not holding speed, so the pitch sags and recovers the way a worn tape deck does. A sound that never drifts is the clearest giveaway that it came out of a computer. This is the last thing on the sound rulebook that nothing in the game was doing. Play it against the steady one and tell me if it is too sick or not sick enough.

items.title: THE SIGNS AT NIGHT
items.why: The three you killed, re-done at night. You were right: I drew signs that still work, in daylight, where a lit sign is invisible, and nothing in any frame was wrong. Now every light has a lamp you can point at and every frame has one wrong thing written under it.
items.said: Not analog horror enough good idea re-cook

items.title: THE RIG ON THE ROOF
items.why: You said it: mfs charge batteries. Right now only a faction holding a lit wire can make one, and no person in the valley ever can. This is the thing that fixes it, drawn: a scavenged panel on angle iron, a cable to a car battery, and four cells in the bays. The cells are the only warm thing on the roof. Right for the valley, or not?

items.title: THE SHOP THAT IS OPEN (THE REDO YOU ASKED FOR)
items.why: You said the last shop was not analog horror enough, so I went and read the art chat's rules and I broke two of them. Rule one says the picture has to be NORMAL except ONE thing that is wrong. My last one had six wrong things: a torn awning, dead trees, a cracked lot, a blank sign, faded paint. Six wrong things is just a ruin, and a ruin is boring. Rule seven says the wrong thing has to be TRUE, from the game, not painted. I had painted the empty shelves because seven looked about right. So here it is the other way round. Everything is normal now: the awnings are fine, the trees are alive, the paint is fresh, the sign is lit and has writing on it. Nothing to look at. And ONE thing is wrong: the shop is open, the lights are on, and there is nothing on any shelf. And it is real now. The game says that block has 3.35 days of food left, so 5 of the 7 shelf runs are bare and 2 still have something. If the food changes, the picture changes. Thumbs up and this is how I cook from now on. Thumbs down and tell me if it is still not scary or if it is now too plain.

items.title: THE GROUND YOU FIGHT ON
items.why: The fight was drawing the grey street from before it was fixed. This is the same board on the street you actually walk, plus the kerb and gutter you approved and nothing has ever drawn. Same layout, only the pictures on the ground changed. Good, or keep looking?

items.title: THE RUNWAY CLOTHES WERE ALREADY HANGING THERE AND NOBODY WORE THEM
items.why: You said the thirteen need redoing to Rick Owens, Balenciaga and Bottega. Turns out we already had 26 clothes cut exactly that way and 22 of them were worn by NOBODY. Zero on the thirteen. You were looking at chore coats and work pants while a cocoon coat hung on the rail. That is my fault, not the art's. I also found the reason nobody could wear them: every one was cut in grey, slate, ash or bone, and your factions ARE their colours, so dressing Blues in slate is against your own colour law. So I cut 12 of those same shapes in the faction colours, one line each, no new drawing. Bottom row is the result. BEING STRAIGHT WITH YOU: only 5 of 13 actually moved, so this is NOT all thirteen redone. Eight of them are defined by having no coat at all, and giving them one would wreck the thing that makes them tell apart. Doing all thirteen properly means rebuilding the whole set from scratch with these clothes in the mix, which is the next round.

items.title: EVERY PERSON IN THE VALLEY HAD THE SAME EYES
items.why: You said way more face customization before anybody hands you a face. So I counted every dial across 400 people. EYE WIDTH HAD ONE VALUE, six, for everybody who has ever existed here, and eye height had two. This is the range now. Not a face to approve, the system getting wider.

items.title: THE HAND AT THE FACE (THIS ONE PLAYS)
items.why: You killed the last one because I showed you pictures instead of the animation. This one plays, on the real beat, killed on the left and redone on the right, in the two directions you called out. Five clips: eat, drink, smoke, cough, whistle. They all aimed with the helper the GUN clips use, so his hand sat about a whole head away from his face in every direction. Still not in the game: the arm that reaches his mouth crosses his throat in profile and cuts his head off his body, and I am fixing that first.
items.said: How dare you show me pictures of animations and not the fucking actual Animation never fucking do that ever again it looks like all of them Northeast and south tweaking

items.title: NOBODY STANDS ON ANYBODY
items.why: You said people were on top of each other on each other's ass. Same street, same second, before and after, off the real screen. Zero stacked bodies at every hour of the day now, and the street did not get emptier to buy it. The names moved toward the county too, like you asked.

items.title: THE GROUND RULER
items.why: A default the manager took for you: an old rule said ground tiles must be busier than the street you already approved, so it failed your own art. New rule: your approved street is the ruler, nothing has to be busier than it. Thumb UP keeps it. Thumb DOWN means you want the ground busier and we re-cook toward more detail.

items.title: THE RING ROAD
items.why: The beltway. Turns out the map has been drawing this ring around the whole valley the entire time and calling it a freeway, so the name showed up on zero cells. This is what one piece of it looks like: six lanes, the barrier down the middle, the sound wall, and the sand that has come over the white line and taken a lane back. Right for the valley, or not?

items.title: THE DARK INSTITUTIONS
items.why: More of the monument you kept. I counted it off the map: the courthouse, police, fire house, library, jail, prison, hospital and cemetery are eighteen blocks and NOT ONE has power. The data fort has all six of its blocks lit.

items.title: HOW LOW THE ROOM
items.why: You voted the room hum up and said the volume has to be very, very low, seven times over. It was only 4 dB under your heartbeat sound, which is why it read loud. I cut it by 22 dB, to a fifth of the loudness. Here it is three ways, one tap each: A is what ships now, B is half again quieter, C is the one you heard. Turn your phone up first, they are all quiet on purpose. Pick the one you stop noticing.
options: C, back to what I heard

items.title: THE EDGE THAT DRUMS
items.why: The strip down the side of every fight was ONE picture repeated fourteen times, because the pool had one tile in it. Now it has eight. No new art: the kerb you approved is one of your sidewalks with a lip on the bottom rows, so I gave that same lip to your other sidewalks. Better, or leave it?

items.title: THE LANE LINE DRUMS TOO
items.why: The painted lines repeated the same way the kerb did: two pictures for the lane, three for the centre line. Now eight and nine. The paint is still yours pixel for pixel, only the road underneath it changes, the way a real road gets patched under a straight line. Better, or leave it?

items.title: THE TOWER THAT IS STILL STANDING
items.why: The map has named a cell THE STRATOSPHERE for months and nothing could build it, so walking there found bare ground. This is it: the tower, the pod, the casino roof, the empty car park. From above you cannot see that a thing is 350 metres tall, so the shadow does the talking and it runs off the far side of the block. Nothing on the plot is lit. Right for the valley, or not?

items.title: THE BIGGEST SCREEN EVER BUILT
items.why: The Sphere. The map gave it four cells and nothing could build it, so walking there found bare dirt. 157 metres of ball in a 192 metre plot, which is why it got four cells and the others got one. From straight above a ball and a disc are the same circle, so the light falling off it does all the work. A million lamps in that surface and not one of them lit. Right for the valley, or not?

items.title: FOOTSTEPS THAT LEAD YOU SOMEWHERE
items.why: Your words: pixel art of footsteps that lead you to the conclusion. One boot at eight times, then the same boot walking across the road, the sidewalk, a dust yard and a flat roof at the size you actually see it. A print is a hole, not a stain, so it is lit by the same sun as everything else and it borrows the ground's own colours. The freshest print is the deepest. Right, or keep going?

items.title: THE STREET THAT IS STILL LIT
items.why: One block at night. You told me my last shop was not analog horror enough, so this time I went and read the art chat's rules FIRST and then asked the game for a real thing to draw instead of making one up. Their rule seven says the scare is lights on where nobody lives, taken from the real world data and never faked. So I counted it: 264 bits of street in this valley still have power, and 168 OF THEM HAVE NOBODY LIVING ON THEM. That is already true in your game right now and nothing on screen tells you. This is one of those blocks, a real one, at 59,4, on MOB's power. Everything in the picture is normal: night, dark houses, a street lamp doing its job. ONE thing is wrong and it is the third house: the lights are on inside and the game says nobody lives there. Nothing points at it. Thumbs up and I put lit empty houses on the real map so you can walk up to one. Thumbs down and tell me if it is too quiet or not the right kind of wrong.

items.title: A NEW THIRTEEN, BUILT RUNWAY FROM THE START
items.why: You said the thirteen all need redoing. I found out why they were workwear and it was not taste: the search that picked them could only choose from dusters, work coats, vests and packs. There was not one runway cut in the box, and no boots in it at all. So I put the runway cuts in the box and ran the same search again. This is what it picked. Nobody chose these by eye. They are 5.6 times more different from each other than the thirteen you voted down, measured the same way, and all thirteen carry a runway cut. Shapes only for now, colour and faces after you rule on the shapes. Do these read as your valley?

items.title: THE FLIP BETWEEN THE THREE ACTS: ON THE PHONE, OR A PLACE
items.why: You said play all three acts at once and flip between them, and you left how open. Two ways. A: the phone shows your three descendants' faces, tap a face and you are them, one tap from anywhere, same screen and same buttons. B: a place in the world, one per district, you walk to it to flip, like the sword pedestal in Ocarina of Time. Default is A: it is instant, it is in your hand, and it does not teleport you to a different mode. Vote up for A, down for B.

items.title: THE THREE DESCENDANTS: NAMED AT THE START, OR WHEN YOU FIRST MEET THEM
items.why: You said name them, male or female, at the start probably, or maybe early in each act. Two ways. A: one screen before act 1, you type all three names and pick male or female for each, so you know whose face you are tapping from minute one. B: you name each one the first time you flip to them. Default is A. Vote up for A, down for B.

items.title: THE ELDER STOOPS
items.why: You said the old person looks like shit, and here is the real reason: the rig had no way to bend a back. Young, middle aged and old were the same body within three percent, and all we could do was make him slightly shorter. He has one bend point now, above the hips, so his back rounds and his head hangs forward. He is 11.6 percent shorter than the middle one instead of 3, and his legs never move. Playing here in all eight directions, and it is in the game.
items.said: the old person looks like shit

items.title: EIGHT DIALS THE GAME HAD AND YOU COULD NOT TOUCH
items.why: You said more face customization before anybody hands you a face. I swept every setting the face has and counted the pixels each one moves. Thirteen of twenty seven were not on the panel. These eight really change the picture, so they are on it now. The maker went from 14 sliders to 22. Nothing invented, they already existed. It is in the CHARACTER tab.

items.title: DOES A RUN SOUND LIKE A RUN
items.why: I measured your walk in the real game before making anything. One press of the pad carries you a whole house, 25 squares, and makes one footstep sound. That is right, it is your own rule. But holding the pad makes you run, and a run covers TWO houses in one beat and still makes ONE sound, so running sounds exactly like walking while you move twice as fast. A is walking, B is running the way it should sound, C is running the way it sounds now (identical to A, which is the bug). Turn the beat on and tell me which one running should be.
options: B, two footfalls a beat when I run

items.title: SOMEBODY STOPS YOU AT YOUR OWN DOOR
items.why: You killed my last two because they were pages of writing. This is the thing itself, shot off the real game on a phone. You walk out of your own door and a woman is standing there. She has a name under her feet, Estella, and she says one line to you and then she is gone. No card, nothing pops up, nothing to close. What she wants is real: the shelf she is talking about is genuinely empty in the market, and the place she points you at is genuinely east of you. Thumbs up and every ask in the game arrives like this. Thumbs down and tell me if it is her, the words, or the fact that she walks off. ONE THING IN THE PICTURE IS WRONG AND I AM NOT HIDING IT: the little face inside her speech bubble is not her. Her body is the girl below it. Every person in the valley has this problem right now, it is not part of what you are voting on, and it is written up.

items.title: THE PHONE IN YOUR POCKET
items.why: Walking around, you had no phone. It only appeared when you zoomed out to the city, and since you killed the phone button there was no way in at all. Now the phone is on you the whole time: folded into the top right corner, 46 by 62, cracked glass with the hour lit behind it and a gold rim when something is unread. Tap it and it opens, same phone, on the street or in the city. No new button was added. Thumbs up and it stays. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the corner it sits in, the size, or that you do not want to see a phone while you walk.

items.title: ONE STORY, THREE MOUTHS
items.why: One man did not pay somebody back. Three tellings later your street believes a different man beat somebody up. Three pictures off the real screen, same street, same mouth. Your city used to pass stories around word for word forever, and the line where somebody says 'probably the wrong version' had never once been true. Four dials underneath: how fast the place goes, the hour goes, the story grows, and the blame moves. They are yours.

items.title: THE LAST LIGHT
items.why: The Volunteers hold 331 blocks of this valley and exactly ONE has power. Here is that block. Only 3.9% of the whole valley is lit, the Cartel hold 17% of all of it, and both substations are dark.

items.title: WHAT A FLIP SOUNDS LIKE
items.why: You said the three acts are open at once and you flip between them on the phone. This is the sound of that flip, and it is not a whoosh. It is a radio changing station: when a radio loses one station and has not found the next, the hiss gets LOUDER, because the machine turns its own volume up hunting for something to receive. Every radio does that. And that gap is the future you have not built yet, so the thinner the act you flip into, the longer it hunts and the louder it gets. A is an act you have lived, B is half built, C is a ruin, which is where you start. Every one is over inside one beat because you tap it constantly. Tell me if the hunt should be shorter, longer, or gone.
options: Keep it, the hunt is right

items.title: THE HAND IS IN FRONT NOW
items.why: Your line from 9/7, answered: facing away, his hand at his mouth really is behind his own skull, so the game never drew it. His hand sat 45 pixels from his face and his whole head is 22 pixels tall. The clip now says out loud that this is a hand at the face and the drawing order reads it, same as the gun clips already do. Under 7 pixels now, every direction, all five clips. Straight with you: this fixes the directions you did NOT name. North-east and south are still on my list and they are about how it moves, not where the hand is.
items.said: when it’s facing north-east the hand was behind the head even though it’s supposed to be in front

items.title: THE SAME CORNER, A HUNDRED YEARS ON
items.why: You said the future should be built out of what you did in the past, and that early on it is a ruin. Nobody had drawn that ruin yet. This is one corner of a street, twice, same camera: on the left how it stands, on the right the same corner a hundred years later after a past that did nothing. It is one drawing, not two. A hundred years takes the soft things away and cracks the hard ones, so the house is gone and the street is breaking up, and the wall and the sidewalk are still perfectly straight with nobody left to use them. Does that ruin read, or is it too clean?

items.title: THE GROUND TELLS YOU WHAT HAPPENED
items.why: You asked for footsteps that lead you to the conclusion. Last round I drew the boot. This round the ground says a whole sentence, and you should be able to read it without me telling you: he walked in, he stood there a while, he ran for it, he went down, and something pulled him back. Five marks, all cut from the one boot. A walk is the whole sole with the feet on two lines. A run is only the front of the sole, because at speed the heel never lands, and the two lines close up to one. Standing is a pair side by side, pressed deeper. Going down is a crescent where the boot turned in place. The drag is two scored furrows with a heel at the head of each. Every mark is a hole in the dirt lit by the same sun as your kerb, in the dirt's own colours, so nothing is a sticker. Thumbs up and the ground starts keeping marks. Thumbs down and tell me which mark you cannot read.

items.title: THE ONE WHO STOOD THERE
items.why: You do not inherit a bill, you inherit the people he owed. Your father borrowed power and did not bring it back, one man watched, and one generation later NOBODY in the game knew. The game even said it: 'died with the last person who saw them'. That man is your neighbour and he is not dead, he is at his door. Now he is still there and he says it once, to your face, and then never again. It cuts both ways: the man your father did a favour for says that too. Nothing pops up and no number moves.

items.title: WHEN A PERSON DIES OF OLD AGE: GONE PAST 70 IN THE NEXT ACT
items.why: The game had a rule waiting on you: when does a person die of old age. Nothing ages anybody out, so the man your father owed is still at his door thirty years later, which is fine if he was 38 and wrong if he was 60. Default: thirty years pass between acts, and a person is gone in the next act if they would be past 70 there. A crashed valley is not a place people get old in. Up keeps 70. Down and tell me the number, or tell me nobody dies.

items.title: THE SHIFT IS LOGGED, AND THERE IS NOBODY TO HAND THE CARD TO
items.why: This came out of something I measured this round, not out of my head. I pressed SCAVENGE in your game with one real finger. It took 477 minutes off your day, almost eight hours, paid you, and the only thing that told you was the clock going from 6:00 to 13:57. So I asked the game who that work belongs to. You work at 48,48 in the suburb, the power under it is DEAD, and NOBODY OWNS THAT GROUND. Across the whole valley, 3,449 blocks have a landlord and 5,767 have nobody. So here is the place that shift happens: a house being pulled apart, roof half off, salvage and pipe stacked on the lot, a barrow. All of it ordinary. ONE thing is wrong and it is the only lit thing in the picture: THE TIME CLOCK BY THE GATE IS STILL RUNNING, and it has punched your shift at 7:57 for an owner who does not exist. The 7:57 is the game's real number. Thumbs up and I build the work site into the street so you can walk up to it. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the place or the idea.

items.title: THE VALLEY AT NIGHT
items.why: Both of these are the whole valley after dark with the SAME number of street lights on. Left is what the game makes right now: the light is sprinkled evenly everywhere, 178 separate little patches, and the biggest lit thing in Las Vegas is twelve squares. Right is what your own light law says (you locked it back in July: the lights go out in CLUSTERS, never every other one), same lights, 11 patches, the biggest one 104 squares. Right gives you real lit neighbourhoods and real dark between them. Which Las Vegas do you want at night?

items.title: THE WHEEL THAT STOPPED
items.why: The map has seven famous Vegas places on it that nothing could ever build, so if you walk to one you find bare dirt. I have drawn four now. This is the High Roller, the giant wheel. Here is the thing I found before I drew a line: the wheel is 143 metres across and the map gives it 96 metres of ground. It does not fit, and it is not supposed to. A third of it hangs out over the neighbours. And from straight above a wheel standing on edge is not a circle, it is a LINE, so what you get is a bright stripe with glass balls beaded along it, four legs leaning in to hold up the axle, and one leg planted on the far side of the road, which is what the real one does. The rim never touches the ground at all. It hangs 25 metres up. The only way to see what shape the thing is is the shadow lying across the yard. Thumbs up and I do the pyramid next. Thumbs down and tell me if it is too big, too empty, or just not readable.

items.title: THE ONES NOBODY CAME FOR
items.why: A hundred years pass and 3,415 blocks of 9,216 get a new owner. That is 37% of the valley. But of the 21 civic blocks, the courts, the jail, the prison, the hospital, the cemetery, the police, the fire house, the library, the chapel and the radio station, exactly ZERO change hands, and every one is dark in both lives. So this is three roadside boards at night: one stamped over because 697 blocks went from the Network to the Mob, one where somebody struck the tier out with a pen, and one that has never been corrected at all. Nobody wrote any of these numbers. They fall out of the two power columns that have been sitting in your faction file since before this chat existed. Thumbs up and I do the rest of the valley this way. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the board, the night, or the stamp.

items.title: HER NAME AND HER FACE
items.why: Estella Gaines stopped you at your own door with a face that looked like an old man. Your game does not know who is a man and who is a woman: not the person, not the body, not the name list, not the face. A name was the only thing in that picture saying 'she' and nothing was listening. Ten of the fifty-eight people on your block wore a haircut that fought their own name. Now none do, and nothing was forced: six of your eleven cuts are still worn by anybody. Same people, same seed, before and after.

items.title: THE KID WALKS
items.why: You said yes to kids and old people on the street. Every age thing I have shown you so far was a still picture, and you told us never to do that again, so this one actually plays. A kid, a teenager and a grown man walking at 120 beats a minute, one step per beat, same clothes, same scale, feet on one line. There is a side view underneath where you can really see the step. The old man is not in it on purpose, and the page tells you why: the game's old man is the same body as a young man give or take three per cent, and that three per cent is actually correct, because real people barely shrink. He needs a bent back, which the animation chat is building. Do the kid and the teen read right?

items.title: THE FACE AT REST
items.why: You said more analog horror fourteen times. The rule behind that phrase is one line: an ordinary picture with exactly ONE thing wrong, and you have to be able to say what the wrong thing is in one sentence. Here is the sentence. HIS EYES ARE POINTED A LITTLE PAST YOUR SHOULDER. Same person on both sides, same face, same hair, same skin, nothing else touched, and they play so you can watch them hold. About one person in twelve. No filter, no monster, no new colour. Is that the kind of wrong you meant, or do you want it further?

items.title: THE SURER, THE WRONGER
items.why: The street gossips about people who are not you and it gets things wrong: the wrong man, a bigger crime, the place gone, the night gone. It said the same two sentences for every one of those, 749 times out of 800. Now the more wrong a story is, the SURER the person sounds saying it, because nobody in the chain knows the wrong man got blamed, so nobody warns you. Three tellings out, she says she was there. She is not lying. AND THE NAMES ARE FIXED: you said "wtf is the watch", so nobody gets called a job word the game never taught you. They get called what they actually do, and you can walk over and check every one of those. Six pictures, all the real game, same street, same woman.

items.title: THE SAME MAN, THE SAME STREET, THE SAME SIZE
items.why: You said the combat was in a different world than the demo. Here is the man in a fight, before and now, next to the man you walk around as. He used to be drawn a third of himself, and then half again because the fight's screen counted pixels differently than the street's, and then he changed size AGAIN every time the camera pulled back to fit somebody in. Now he is one size, the same one you walk around as, and he stays that size no matter how far the camera pulls back. The ground still zooms. He does not. The floor under him is your own approved street art, not the fight's private copy. Thumbs up and I keep going on the fight's feel. Thumbs down and tell me if he is too big, too small, or if it is the ground I should be looking at instead.

items.title: THE PHONE WHILE IT WAKES UP
items.why: You tapped the phone and got a black rectangle for a moment, the same thing that happened to you with the door. Both pictures are the real phone in the city view, same touch, same glass, same run: left is what you got, right is what you get now. The phone's page is 2 megabytes and takes a beat to arrive, so while it comes the phone wears its own face: the hour it already knows, where you are standing, and a dead network that is still looking. You said the phone belongs in the city view only and it is back to city only. Thumbs up and this stays. items.title: FACING YOU, HE WAS DOING NOTHING
items.why: The last two clips from that old batch you never gave a thumb to: picking something up, and laughing. Before showing them I looked, and they were broken in a way nobody had measured. A man who bends over disappears when he faces you, because bending forward is a sideways move and there is nothing to show from the front. Picking something up changed 126% of his pixels from the side and 36% facing you, and moved his body ten pixels from the side against less than one facing you. Laughing facing you moved him ONE pixel. He was standing still. Now the squat is spent where it shows: he drops, his legs fold, his arms and head go down. A laugh is a bounce and a shake. 5.5 pixels instead of 0.9, and 4.2 instead of 1.0. From the side both are untouched. This one PLAYS.

items.title: A FOOTSTEP THAT IS NOT SAND
items.why: You were right and here is why. Every sound I made started with a noise generator, and noise with the top cut off is exactly what sand sounds like. Measuring it properly this round, the old footstep leaks 28 percent of itself above the limit it was supposed to stop at, and that leak IS the sand. So A on the page is the one you called sand, unchanged, so you can hear it next to the new one. B and C have NOT ONE noise generator in them: they are built from the physics of a heel hitting a slab. The click is the contact, less than half a millisecond on concrete because concrete is stiff, and that is what makes it bright. Under it the slab rings at a pitch that comes out of concrete's own published stiffness, not out of me picking. Then a couple of dozen grains of grit crush under the heel, each one its own tiny impact, which is where the grain comes from instead of hiss. C is the same thing on asphalt, which is ten times softer, so the road thuds where the sidewalk rings. You are hearing the material. Tell me if it is still sand.
options: B and C, that is a footstep

items.title: THE SAME STREET, RECLAIMED (ACT TWO OF THE ONE YOU LIKED)
items.why: You thumbed up THE STREET THAT IS STILL LIT, so here is the exact same block at the next date. Same four houses, same road, same lamp, same coordinates, 59,4 on MOB's power. Nothing redrawn from scratch. You just said the ruin is the FLOOR and it only gets better from there, never worse, so act two is act one PLUS what got reclaimed: the road is patched, the power is back on the street, there is a panel array and a battery cabinet on the first roof, and the line is restrung to the pole. All of it is stuff added, nothing taken away. AND ONE THING IS STILL WRONG. The whole street came back with new cold modern light, and the empty house is still sitting there with the same old warm bulb, exactly as it was. Everything around it got better. It did not. First go at this I lit every house the same warm colour and the wrong thing vanished into the improvement, which taught me something: if everything gets better in the same way the wrong thing already was, you stop being able to see it. Thumbs up and this is how all three acts get drawn. Thumbs down and tell me if act two should look more different than this.

items.title: WHICH WAY IS HE FACING
items.why: You said: find out when it's facing north south east and west. And: don't have it be exactly a straight line. Both done. There are eight facings now and every one is DRAWN at that angle instead of a bitmap spun round, which is why the diagonal ones stopped looking chewed up. The toe half is your boot, pixel for pixel, untouched. Two things I found while doing it, and you should look hard at both. ONE: your boot is the same width at both ends and both ends taper the same, so north and south came out as the SAME print and the ground never said which way he went. The heel is thinner and flat now. Both boots are on the card side by side, so say the word and the old heel goes back. TWO: every row of the old mask was a mirror of itself, so the left and right boots were literally the same boot and a trail has been laying one foot twice this whole time. The arch is on the inside now, so left and right lean away from each other. items.title: THE HOLE IN THE SCREEN
items.why: You said the square in the bottom left was clipping on top, and asked for a tiny hole in the roof if I could make it look good. Both done. You were right about the square and the cause was stupid: it was drawn after the service road, so it ATE the road and ended up sitting straight against the ball with nothing in between. Moving it was not enough either, because there is a three tile gap between the ball and the road and the corner was landing in that. It is clipped to outside the road now, its corner is cut by the curve, and it has a kerb and loading bays so it reads as a yard and not a grey block. The hole is 12 metres across on a 157 metre ball. The inside is the darkest thing on the plot, because there is nothing behind a screen. The sun catches the torn lip, same sun as everything else.

items.title: YOU CANNOT SEE TERRITORY

Zoom out to the city and you can see none of it at all, just blank sand. A sign was never going to fix that. A sign is one building and this is the whole valley. items.title: A BLOCK CHANGED HANDS
items.why: Until this round no block in this valley could EVER change owner. Now a block can change hands and be remembered, per life, so your third generation can inherit what your first one took. Here is the first one, one step west of your front door: Mob to Volunteers, fortress ground stays fortress ground, your own block untouched. Both pictures are photographs of your real game. AND YOU CANNOT SEE IT, which is the honest half: the street never says a word, and out in the city view the game asks who owns the ground exactly ZERO times. items.title: THE CAMP THAT HOLDS THE POWER
items.why: You said the overworld is Battle Brothers and places are destinations. So I went and counted what a place in our valley actually gives you when you turn up, and the answer is bad: fourteen places, THREE shelves. Every camp sells the same four things. And here is the one that got me: the Homeless are second from the bottom of your power list, they are a camp, they sell the shortest list in the valley, and they are sitting on 254 of the 308 squares that make power. The poorest place in Las Vegas makes the most money and sells the least. This is that place, drawn: the shacks, and the panel field they live off. items.title: THE BUST

The cause turned out to be a bug, not taste: our shoulders are one fixed shape drawn at the same height on every face, while the chin above them moves twelve rows across the crowd and now moves whenever you drag your own sliders. On a short face that leaves a long bare neck. These sit under the chin they belong to. It is honest about its size: 145 of 200 people get less empty space, the middle one gains 2 points, the best gains 12, and a long face is unchanged. It is OFF until you say, because it reframes every face in the game. Worth turning on?

items.title: THE MAP HAS MARKERS

So here are the first five things that go on the valley map, and every one of them moves. First though, the measurement: the map you have right now has NO marker of any kind on it. It paints the ground and draws one search dot. You cannot see where you are or where anything is. These five are YOU with a banner, a shop, a shed, a pump and a fortress. They are drawn in the map's own colours, dark with one bright mark each, because that is the only thing you can find from across a valley. Each one has ONE part that moves and feet that never do: your banner stirs while you travel and hangs dead when you stop, the shop sign keeps trying to light and cannot hold it, a loose roof sheet on the shed lifts and drops, the pump beam is still nodding with nothing on the other end of it, and a watch light comes round the fortress towers so somebody is still up there. items.title: THE BUTTON YOUR THUMB FINDS

items.title: THE THREE ARE ON YOUR PHONE

Zoom out to the map and the cracked phone has three faces along the bottom: Reyna, now. Ezekiel, thirty five years later. Perla, seventy years later. The one you are is lit. items.title: PICK YOUR MAN OUT
items.why: Battle Brothers puts your whole company in a grid of little faces and you find your guy without thinking, so I asked whether you can find yours. While asking I found the game's own checker had been calling two of your people THE SAME PERSON for four rounds, and I kept repeating it. They are not: they differ in four things you can name, and one of them is wearing sunglasses. The checker was adding up brightness, which is not how anybody tells faces apart. Fixed, and measured properly: of all 1,770 pairs of sixty people, not one pair shares every single thing about them. Here are nine of yours at the real size, picked to match the crowd and not to flatter it, and they move, which a Battle Brothers roster cannot do. Can you tell them apart, and does the fact that 29% of the valley has its eyes behind shades bother you?

items.title: FOURTEEN CREWS, NONE ON THE MAP
items.why: You just ruled that the overworld IS the Battle Brothers map, which makes the zoomed out screen the most important one in the game. In Battle Brothers you look at that map and you instantly know who owns what, because every town flies its house's colours, and watching those colours change hands IS the story. Here is a photograph of OUR map on the running game. Fourteen crews own every block of this valley, all fourteen have a seat out there, every one has a colour you picked yourself off clothes you approved, AND YOU CAN SEE NONE OF IT. The one number that settles it: I put a counter on the question the game asks when it wants to know who owns a block. On the street it asks two or three times a second. Out on the map it asks ZERO times. It does not paint territory badly, it never asks. Thumbs up and I put the crews on the map. Thumbs down and the map stays sand.

items.title: THE SAME VALLEY, THREE ACTS
items.why: You said the future gets better, and that the map at the later acts is the same roads with the fill worked out from what you did. This is that, from the map camera, at night. Same valley three times. Left is what the game actually ships right now. Middle and right are what it looks like after people claw parts of it back. NOTHING is ever switched off: every light on in one panel is on in the next. And every road, mountain and lot line is the SAME, not redrawn: I compared 6,899 ground pixels across the three and zero of them moved. The creepy part is on purpose: the dark never changes shape, so it is not a city growing, it is a city being switched back on inside a body that stayed the same. Does the future getting better look like this?

items.title: THE VALLEY READS AS LAND
items.why: You made the overworld Battle Brothers. So I rendered the valley at the zoom you actually cross it at and looked. IT IS A GRID OF GREY SQUARES WITH BLACK LINES THROUGH IT. Roads are 38 percent of every cell in the valley and all of them are one near black. Everything built is the same grey. The mountains are a tenth of the map and you cannot see them at all. So on the one screen you are supposed to travel across, you cannot tell city from desert from mountain, and the only thing you CAN see is the street grid. That is backwards. Three changes, left picture is now, right picture is this. The land gets its own range so the mountains ring it, the open ground is warm, and the city is quiet inside its own grain because you are IN the city, you do not navigate by it. The street grid drops to a whisper, because at a quarter of the map it cannot be the subject. And the ridges catch the sun on their north west faces, same sun as every pixel in the game, which is what turns a dark patch into a mountain. The dust drifts across the open ground, one cell a beat. Thumbs down and tell me if it is too dark, too flat, or if you want your grid back.

items.title: THE FIGHT IS STILL A DIFFERENT GAME
items.why: You said one game mode, no teleporting, the buttons never change. Here is where that actually stands, measured, not guessed. Both shots are the real game in one run, seconds apart: I walked up to a crew and tapped them. LEFT is walking, with the bar, the notes button and the walk pad ringed. RIGHT is the fight. Every one of those is gone. Not moved, gone. The walk has 9 things on screen, the fight has 30, and they do not share a single one, because the fight is a separate page. And one number nobody had counted: of the fight's own buttons, only SHOOT is big enough to press with a thumb. The eight little compass dots are 28 pixels. Your reach is 44. This is not me asking you to approve anything, it is the before picture, and the fight lane already has this row open and agrees. What I am building toward: the ground under you lights up for reach, the walk pad you already hold carries the enemy's beat, the bar says whose turn it is, the phone tells you afterwards what it cost, and ONE new thing for the weapon you are holding. Thirty things become five, and four of them already exist.

items.title: THE GRID: A CELL IS 32 PIXELS, YOU ARE ONE CELL, A HOUSE IS ABOUT 4 BY 4
items.why: You said the character stays tiny and moves one grid at a time, and one house does not equal one tile. Default sizes so everyone builds the same grid: a cell is about 32 pixels on your phone (about 11 across the screen), you fit in one cell, a house is about 4 by 4 cells with a door and an inside, a car is 2 by 1, a street is 3 cells wide with a 1-cell sidewalk each side. Every cell is one of five things: floor, wall, door, cover, prop. Up keeps these. Down and say which number is wrong.

items.title: THE ONLY HIGH GROUND IN THE FIGHT
items.why: You made one call about ground in a fight: ONE terrain rule, high ground helps you aim, and nothing else on a tile changes a number. I went and checked what the game already builds for that, and this is it, photographed in a real fight I walked into off the street. Then I counted it over 120 fights. A tile is one house, 12 metres. The raised slab turns up in 71% of fights. IT IS NINE HOUSES ACROSS, about 111 metres, so it is a city block with a staircase, not a mound. The nearest way up is 6 houses away. You start on the ground 120 times out of 120. So the one rule you kept changed 0 of 519 shots. It has never once fired in a fight anybody has played. The good news is there is nothing to delete: the game never grew Battle Brothers' hills and swamps and forests, so high ground really is the only ground rule in here. What I want to do next is make it a MOUND: something small, one house, that you are standing on or one step away from, so taking the height is a move you make in the fight instead of a building across the street. And when you are up on it you should SEE it, not read a plus sign. Thumbs up and I build the mound that way. Thumbs down and tell me if you would rather keep the big raised block and just make it reachable.

items.title: HOW YOU CROSS THE MAP
items.why: You said the valley gets crossed the Battle Brothers way, a marker you send somewhere while the clock runs. FIRST, WHAT THE MAP DOES NOW: I pressed the walk pad twenty-four times in all eight directions while zoomed out and he moved ZERO. The same press on the street moves him twenty-two lots and shifts three quarters of the screen. There is no marker and the pad is dead out there. So how should it travel? Battle Brothers slides its marker smoothly in real time and lets you pause. Your own rule says everything moves on the beat, twice a second, street and city both, one game mode. Those cannot both be true. A is their way, B is on the beat, and I picked B and built it because it is your own two rules agreeing and it is the walk feel you already voted for. They cover the SAME ground: B just stops at every beat and moves twice as fast in between. Say A and I switch it.
items.said: the valley is crossed on a MAP the Battle Brothers way: a party marker, tap where to go, time passes

items.title: THE ONLY PUMP
items.why: The Battle Brothers revamp says a place is a block and its buildings are what it offers. I built that and then counted the valley: 467 blocks, 215 of them offer nothing at all, and the ones that do are 249 shops, 12 sheds, 7 fortresses and ONE PUMP. The whole valley drinks through a single block. Battle Brothers towns have three to eight things attached to them; ours have one or none. So this is that block, from the camera you play on: two pumps, the pipes, the fence, the gate shut. The wrong thing is the path. There is only one worn into the yard and it goes to the electrical cabinet, not to the pumps. Somebody comes here a lot and only ever touches the switch.

items.title: WHO IS THAT ON THE ROAD
items.why: Parties roam the map now, so I drew all thirteen factions moving on it. TAP THIS, IT PLAYS. But first the thing I found. Your thirteen faction colours are yours, measured off your own clothes, and they stay. I measured what they do as banners on a map. CARTEL AND MOB ARE THE SAME COLOUR. They are 3.6 apart on a scale that goes to 373. Eight more pairs are under 50. And nine of the thirteen are the same brightness as the city ground they would be standing on. Eight of them are brown and four are grey, because this is a valley of working people in dust, which is right. It just means you can never tell who is coming by the colour of the flag. So the SHAPE tells you what they are and the banner tells you who. Four shapes: someone on foot with a flag, a patrol in a rank with points over it, a caravan with a canvas and wheels, and a crowd carrying their bedding. Which faction gets which shape comes from each faction's own canon alignment in the game files, not from me. Thumbs down and tell me which two you still cannot tell apart.

items.title: THE SAME STREET, THREE TIMES
items.why: One block. Three dates. Top is the ruin, which is the picture you already gave a thumb up. Middle is the same street reclaimed: the road patched, the power back, solar on a roof and a battery cabinet beside it, the line restrung. Bottom is the same street paying for itself: a second array across the road, the kerbs and the walks rebuilt, a second lamp, and the dead lot turned into a battery swap stand you can work at night. Nothing is ever taken away between one picture and the next, because you said the ruin is the floor. The machine counts that, it does not just say it. And one thing never changes in any of the three: the third house has its lights on and nobody lives in it, in all three acts. Everything around it gets better twice over and it never does. Thumbs up and this is how the city screen draws the act you are in. Thumbs down and tell me which act is wrong.

items.title: THE THIRTEEN ARE WEARING IT NOW
items.why: You said fire on the thirteen new runway shapes, so the thirteen groups put them on. This page PLAYS: every body walks at the speed the game runs at, standing on the street's own road and sidewalk, at the size the game draws a person. Four of them are here instead of thirteen, because these four are the ones that nearly lost their colour when the new clothes went on. The new clothes were searched on SHAPE, so every one of them came out grey or bone, and dressing everybody in them would have washed the colour out of eleven of thirteen groups in one go. Seventeen new colourways fixed that: same coat, same cut, the group's own colour, one line each, no new art. Nobody lost their colour and nobody changed body. Thumbs up and this is who is on your street. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the cut, the colour, or the boots.

items.title: WHAT THIS VALLEY STRIKES ON THE HOUR
items.why: You said the overworld is Battle Brothers and that time passes while you travel. You also said their map is a bunch of still pictures and we put life into it. So the map gets a clock you can HEAR. None of these three has one noise generator in it, which is the thing you killed three sounds over: they are metal being struck, and the notes inside each one are the real ones. A bell founder tunes a bell to a MINOR THIRD, which is why every bell you have ever heard sounds sad, and that is A and B. A struck pipe is not a chord at all, its notes sit at odd spacings, and that is why it clangs instead of ringing: that is C. A is a cracked bell, which is the realistic one for a valley nobody has maintained in ten years, so it leads. B is the same bell uncracked: its low note rings a second and a half after the high ones have gone, which is why a real bell seems to warm up as it fades. C is no bell at all, just a length of steel pipe, because that is what a dead town actually has. Tell me what this valley strikes.
options: B, a bell that still works

items.title: THE DECK IS NOT THE HISS
items.why: You killed the tape and you said it all sounded like sand. You were right: it was a band of hiss with a machine's name on it. This is the same idea rebuilt out of the machine instead. A tape deck is plastic being knocked and wheels turning, and hiss is the one part of a cassette a phone speaker would never pick up anyway. Press play and you get the lever, the head arriving 45 ms later, and the song SLIDING UP to speed, which is what a real deck does and what a whoosh was standing in for. Nothing in it is a number I picked: the standard says the tape moves 4.7625 cm a second, so the capstan turns 7.58 times a second and the reel 0.69, and those two are the wobble you hear. And the best part is free: the wobble gets SLOWER as the side plays, because the tape piling onto the reel makes it fatter. Same machine, slower breath. That is why a tape sounds tired instead of broken. Zero noise generators in it.
options: B, just the machine, no song

items.title: A FLIP IS A TAPE CHANGING
items.why: You said the old flip was kinda dogshit. It was hiss too, and it also claimed to be a radio while being built wider than any radio. This one is what the law already said a flip is: a tape changing. The flip is ONE TAP and it is always there, so you will hear it hundreds of times, which means the way it fails is not too quiet, it is I am sick of it. So: inside one beat, no riser, no whoosh, no sting, just the shell seating and the machine taking it. It is honest about what it is not, too: a real tape change takes several seconds, so this is the part of one you actually hear. The knock is a polystyrene shell ringing its own notes, which come from its shape and not from a setting. Zero noise generators in it.

items.title: THE ONE WHO FELL IN
items.why: Nobody has ever walked with you in this game. Now somebody tells you what they used to be, and if you do not walk off, they come with you. Every picture is the walked street from the game's own camera. Is this the companion you want, and is one at a time right?

items.title: TERRITORY SURVIVES THE REBUILD
items.why: You just asked if we have to restart the whole enchilada for the new honest grid rule. For this lane, no. Territory lives one size up: the valley is 9,216 lots and fourteen crews own them, and that layer is untouched by your new rule, which only rebuilds what is INSIDE one lot (floor, wall, door, a house four cells across). items.title: IT IS NOT THREE GENERATIONS. IT IS THREE CRISES ON ONE MAP.
items.why: Battle Brothers never has generations. A brother dies, you hire another, and the company keeps its name, its crowns, and what every noble house thinks of it. The only thing that changes the world is a CRISIS: a war, an invasion, a plague of undead, that redraws who holds what without ever redrawing the map itself. That is closer to what your three acts already are than 'three lives' is. Same streets in all three, always. What changes is who holds them and what still works, which is exactly a Battle Brothers crisis. Research only, nothing to look at yet.

show.src:
NO GENERATIONS. ONE COMPANY, ONE MAP, THREE CRISIS CHECKPOINTS.

Battle Brothers has no fold, no time skip, no heir screen. Men die constantly and nobody notices, because the company is a name and a ledger, not a body. What changes the world is a CRISIS: same roads, same rivers, same towns, but who holds them and what they need is rewritten.

Our three acts already work this way and did not know it. One seed. One layout, 4,459 bytes, never rewritten. Measured on the real map this round: 6,899 ground pixels compared across all three acts, zero moved. Only what is lit and who owns it differs.

So stop saying generation. Say crisis checkpoint. Act 1 is before the crisis is answered. Acts 2 and 3 are the same crisis, further along, because the company (you, standing in three bodies) did more about it.

items.title: ONE HOUSE IS NOT ONE TILE
items.why: You said it: one house does not equal one tile, it is all fucked up. So here is the fight board you have right now, on the left, photographed in a real fight I walked into off the street. A tile is a whole house, 12 metres, and your phone holds TWO of them. That is why a fight feels like standing in a car park. On the right is the same picture with the new grid drawn on it. A cell is 32 pixels, so the phone holds 12 across and 20 down. A house is 4 by 4 cells, which makes a cell 3 metres and keeps a house at 12 metres, so nothing about the world changes size, only what a step is. Your man goes from 112 pixels to ONE CELL. Now the part worth looking at. The three squares are your reach, and I did not change a single distance you already picked: pistol 4 cells is still 12 metres, rifle 8 is still 24, scope 12 is still 36. Look what happens. Only the pistol fits on the phone. The rifle fills the whole board and the scope runs off the edge. That is not a bug, that is what a rifle actually is, and the fight camera already pulls back to hold everybody, so a rifle fight opens the shot by itself. Thumbs up and I build the fight on these cells. Thumbs down and tell me if your man is too small at one cell, or if a cell should be bigger than 32.

items.title: YOUR CHARACTER GOES SMALL
items.why: You said your character should stay tiny and move one square at a time, like the game used to. This is the first try at that small body. It plays: it is the game's own walk, shrunk down to the exact size a square will be. Nothing here is hand drawn yet, it is the big body run through a shrinking machine, so a hem or a stripe is gone but the shape and the colour are not. Seven people from seven different groups, each one still readable as themselves and still their own colour, measured, not guessed. Thumbs up and this is the road small bodies go down while somebody draws them by hand. Thumbs down and tell me if it is too small, too blurry, or if two of them look the same.

items.title: HE WALKS AT ONE CELL
items.why: You said the character is tiny again, one cell, one step per cell. First thing I had to answer: cut the big body down to one cell, is there still an animation in there? YES. All eight directions stay eight different pictures, nothing turned to mush, zero stray floating pixels. He is 24 rows tall with 168 lit pixels. The big art stays the source, like you said. BUT IT FOUND SOMETHING BROKEN THE WHOLE TIME, AT EVERY SIZE: the walk is built on a wave, and a wave is at zero twice per step, so frames 1 and 3 came out exactly the same picture on all six side-on directions. The side walk had THREE pictures, not four, and running too. At the big size you might not notice; at one cell it reads as a limp. A real walk's two middles differ because one leg is passing forward and THE PASSING FOOT CLEARS THE GROUND. That is the missing fourth picture and it is how legs work. This one PLAYS, with a panel at his actual size so it cannot flatter itself.
items.said: your character stays tiny even as you zoom out

items.title: STRUCK DOWN IN A FIGHT: 20% DEAD, ELSE OUT FOR 30 TO 40 DAYS WITH A MARK
items.why: Your words: only a 20% chance your character can die, otherwise a debilitating injury. Default: when one of yours is struck down, one in five dies for good and the company remembers. The other four in five live, are out of every fight for 30 to 40 game days, still cost their day, and keep a permanent mark: a scar, a limp, a lost eye, a stat that never comes back. Up keeps 20% and 30 to 40 days. Down and give me the number you want.

items.title: TWO LADDERS, NEITHER READS GROUND
items.why: This valley already tracks two separate numbers for how much a crew trusts you: a favour count, and a rank (TERRITORY up to MANDATE up to MAYOR) that decides where you can even build. Both are real and already on a card you can open. I checked every place either number moves. Both only move because a QUEST resolved. Holding a crew's fortress, losing it, paying their rent on time or missing it: none of that touches either ladder, in either direction. And you just ruled the quest chat ships no more game code, ever, only research, which means both ladders now have exactly one door and it is closing. This lane's own ledger already knows every block that changes hands and has never been asked a single question by either one. Thumbs up and I wire territory into standing. Thumbs down and they stay two separate systems.

items.title: THE WATER YOU COULD STAND ON
items.why: This is not a drawing, it is the dam pulled straight out of the game and coloured by one question: can you stand here. Green means you can walk on it. Grey is something solid. Top picture is what the game actually believed until this round: THE WHOLE RESERVOIR IS RED, and red means you could walk out onto it. A third of that block was water you could stand on, 5,329 squares of it, plus the creek at the fort. It happened because every square has a word saying what it is, one list decides what each word does, and the word water was not on the list. Anything not on the list quietly becomes floor. Bottom picture is the same block after the fix: the water is water again, and nothing else moved, the solid stuff is identical in both. The dry stuff stayed walkable too, so empty fountains and drained pools are still floor like they should be. Thumbs up and the blue is what deep water looks like on the map from now on. Thumbs down and tell me what water should do to you instead.

items.title: WHAT THE BAR SAYS
items.why: The strip across the top of the game says NOTHING right now. I measured it: 390 by 50 pixels of black with one button in it. You said Battle Brothers is the game, and Battle Brothers keeps five numbers on screen every second and never takes them off. You also said less on screen. So this is the one question, asked once. All three phones are the same real shot of the street from the game's own camera, and only the strip changes. A is what you have. B is three readings: batteries, the hour, where you are. C is five, the Battle Brothers count: add the day and who is with you. The gold squares are the new cell size you just set, so you can see the strip costs one and a half rows of world either way, whether it says something or nothing. The readings are already built and switched off, so B and C are a switch, not new work.
